//: Artwork for the demo catalogue DemoWallSeeder ships, as fixtures rather than as generated art.
A demo wall exists to show what the product looks like with inventory on it, and inventory is
recognisable app art. The gradient-and-initial tiles this replaced showed the fallback instead of
the wall, and they showed it in a palette the brand does not own (design.md §2).
Each entry names the exact app: its storefront, its numeric store id, its bundle identifier and the
seller of record. `demo:offer-art` looks the id up, refuses to write unless the bundle and the seller
both match what is written here, and saves the official 512px artwork the store publishes. That is
what makes the art verifiable and the fetch reproducible: a search by name could quietly land on a
similarly named game, and an id alone could be reassigned.
Keyed by `offers.external_id`, not by `offers.id`: the primary key is assigned by the database and
differs between machines, so a fixture named after it would only install on the box that made it.
Square icons only. The store publishes no promotional banner through this endpoint, the rail tile is
aspect-ratio 1, and stretching an icon into a banner is worse than not having one. Offers with no
entry here (the survey, the truncation row) carry no art and render the letter tile, which is also
how a real offer whose network deleted its asset renders.
